threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say 'excuse me' to get past people on the pavements. Trust me, no one here cares about that.
Saw a couple on the 35 last night arguing about whether the man had actually lost his wallet or just left it at home. The driver rolled his eyes.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a kid selling homemade lemonade outside the Kottbusser Tor U-Bahn, with a handwritten sign saying 'Zuckerfrei'.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin will you find a club where the bathroom attendant hands out complimentary mints and advice on how to survive the night.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they're from here if they complain about the BART delays while casually sipping coffee from a local shop, barely fazed.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Last week, a guy serenaded us with a sax on the 38L, and when he hit the high note, even the driver cracked a smile. Weird charm of this city.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the best paella is at the fancy restaurants; the real gems are hidden in the locals-only bodegas, where it's more about the vibe.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new by their hesitant approach to ordering tapas – still asking for ketchup with patatas bravas.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it the ‘Overground’ instead of just ‘the train’ and look confused when it’s packed like a sardine can.
Last night on the 196, a guy serenaded the bus with old school grime tracks. Oddly fitting for the Brixton vibe, everyone just went with it.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a guy in a full lederhosen riding a bike with a parrot on his shoulder near Hermannplatz. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain do you find spontaneous techno parties in abandoned buildings, complete with food stalls and art installations. It's wild.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from here if they can name all the taco places on Mission from 16th to 24th without skipping a beat, even the hole-in-the-walls.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 21 with a guy serenading everyone with a ukulele. Only in SF would a quirky moment like that outshine the usual delays.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but they miss the real vibe in the narrow streets where locals hang out and find the hidden bars.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their reluctance to order anything other than 'café con leche' - they haven't discovered the joy of a simple 'bica' yet.
